# ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry Daily Update (Aug 21, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on registry maintenance, including removing unused fields and scheduling upgrades for World Chain. Automated code generation also updated addresses.json.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Registry Maintenance and Updates
- Removed the `op_contracts_manager_addr` field from the `sepolia-devnet-2` superchain configuration, as it was an unused field [#1304](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1304).
- Scheduled Karst upgrades for World Chain by adding corresponding timestamps to both mainnet and Sepolia configurations [#1313](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1313).
- An automated code generation update modified `addresses.json` [#1312](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1312).

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
No new pull requests were opened today.

## CLOSED ISSUES
No issues were closed today.

## NEW ISSUES
No new issues were reported today.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### Kona Node Service Refactoring and Interop Development
Discussions on [#22527](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22527) (kona-node-service: EngineActor becomes ChainController) and [#22530](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22530) (kona-node-service: shared single-chain composition entry point) highlight ongoing efforts to refactor the `EngineActor` to `ChainController` and create a reusable single-chain composition entry point. Key points include:
- The `EngineActor` refactoring aims to mediate derivation-bound signals and own reset initiation, with a focus on read-only query handling. A new PR [#22597](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22597) was opened for the read-only query handler.
- The query handler's atomicity was clarified, noting that the pairing of L2 block and L1 key is crucial for correctness.
- The `RollupNode::start()` function was split into `compose` and `run_actors` to improve reusability and supervision of multiple chains.
- The L1 watcher is deliberately kept separate from a chain's composition to allow for multi-chain hosts.
- A potential issue with actor error reporting in multi-chain setups was identified, where a dying actor cannot easily identify its chain.

### Lokahi N-Chain Scaffolding and Interop Stores
Progress on [#22521](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22521) (lokahi: N-chain scaffolding without interop (phase 2)) and [#22532](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22532) (lokahi: N-chain service composition and config) indicates the development of a multi-chain node. Key updates include:
- The multi-chain L1 watcher [#22531](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22531) is done, and a shared single-chain composition entry point [#22530](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22530) is open.
- The N-chain composition and config [#22532](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22532) is the first item that will merge these parallel development lines.
- The L1 watcher's fixed, non-empty chain set is confirmed as correct by design, as chains cannot be dynamically added to a running instance.
- The `lokahi` node can now run N chains in one process, with per-chain actor groups, a multi-chain L1 watcher, layered config, and per-chain data directories and RPC sockets.
- A latent test bug related to chain-label assertions was exposed and fixed during the merge.

### Lokahi Interop Verification and RPCs
Discussions on [#22537](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22537) (lokahi: cross-safe promotion lifecycle and finality), [#22535](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22535) (lokahi-interop: stores), [#22536](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22536) (lokahi-interop: verification round loop), [#22544](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22544) (lokahi: supernode_syncStatus and superroot_atTimestamp RPCs), and [#22545](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22545) (lokahi: sequencer mode) detail the implementation of interop verification, persistent stores, and RPC functionalities. Key developments include:
- The interop actor is now wired as the promotion source, with promotions routing through Kona's existing external promoter entry point.
- The `kona-safedb` now records paired local-safe advances and handles rewinds across resets.
- Interop activation is all-or-nothing across the hosted set, requiring all chains to schedule Lagoon at the same timestamp.
- The `lokahi-interop` crate now includes verified, log, and invalidated-output archive stores, with a focus on durability and idempotent replay.
- The verification round loop is implemented, observing chains and L1, making decisions, writing to a WAL, and applying changes.
- The `supernode_syncStatus` and `superroot_atTimestamp` RPCs are being implemented, with deliberate differences from Go's op-supernode in aggregate `current_l1` and handling of invalidated outputs.
- The sequencer mode is enabled, allowing Kona's sequencer to run per chain in Lokahi config, with configuration derived from the presence of sequencer settings.

### Devstack Abstraction and Acceptance Testing
Discussions on [#22546](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22546) (op-devstack: abstract SupernodeTestControl and add lokahi to the acceptance matrix) and [#22547](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22547) (lokahi: Rust multi-chain interop node (tracking)) focus on abstracting the devstack's `SupernodeTestControl` and integrating Lokahi into the acceptance test matrix. Key points include:
- The `SupernodeTestControl` has been made RPC-shaped, allowing out-of-process implementations.
- Adding Lokahi to the acceptance matrix is currently blocked on the completion of interop verifier wiring, `QueryAPI` implementation, and sequencer mode support.
- The `RestartWithFreshDataDir` method was added to `LokahiSupernode`.

### Flaky Test and Op-Supernode Observations
A new issue [#22630](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22630) reports a flaky test `TestSDMActivatesAtLagoonBoundary`, which has been confirmed as a timing-dependent failure. A fix is available in [#22638](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22638) that makes block 1 a deterministic pre-Lagoon workload.

Issue [#22636](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22636) records observations from mirroring op-supernode's behavior in Lokahi, highlighting areas where the copied behavior might not be intended. A significant observation is that the `memory-all-kona-lokahi-op-reth-<fork>` CI job has been running `op-supernode` instead of `lokahi`, leading to false green results. This is being addressed in [#22639](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22639) by renaming the job and reporting the selected supernode kind in the test record.
